Here's why I gave up my beloved Galaxy S7 for a boring old iPhone

I really hate mAh as a unit. Two things wrong with it. What you really want to know is the energy. Use joules or watt hours. At least one of those is something you are familiar with. The reason why mAh is a thing is because eletrical engineers are likely to compare batteries of the same voltage (whatever voltage is needed for their project) so amp hours is fine. But if comparing two batteries with the same voltage watt hours will be just as good. It's just more versitile for comparing capacities.

The other reason it's amp hours is because when actually designing something you can avoid calculating the power multiplying by the voltage drop or calculating i2r. It's less multiplication and therefore less math that saying this diode, or even a series, will draw this many amps at max, something you already have to know about your circuit to not blow it, and I have blank amp hours. So it reduces math after you've bought the battery and are working with it but none of this is a concern to anyone without a schematic in front of them. For just plain putting energy storage into context... use energy.

I looked it up and both are running 3.8V but the problem with mAh is when you read it you have to wonder something like that and it's ambiguity. If people would use 10.5 Wh you wouldn't need to be curious if the power is stored at different voltages. Plus 10.5 Wh is so much more consumer friendly than 2,750 mAh. 10.5 is in the same spectrum of numbers people use to keep track of versions of things. Maybe that's the point. It would make consumers way to good at keeping track of what batteries are good instead of just listening to the tone of the sales person talking to them.
